sense.text: “Behold an horrible vision, and the appearance thereof from the east”. Those who think the Bible is a fairy tale: no, negro, you are the fairy tale. You think the Bible is not real; no, negro. It is happening right now, in the news of this very week, and the media did not cover it.

“The nations of the dragons of Arabia” are the Arabs: Bahrain, Iraq, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Oman, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Syria, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. They “shall come out with many chariots”, “that all they which hear them may fear and tremble.” Why will the world fear? Because they are going to come together and unite. That is what the world is going to fear.

This week Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkey signed the Mecca agreement in Mecca: you attack one, you attack them all, just like NATO. They are starting to unite. Turkey has one of the greatest militaries in the world, and Pakistan has the nuclear weapon. Saudi Arabia had a deal to give America cheap oil in return for America’s protection, and Iran proved America cannot protect them, so now they say, we have to protect ourselves. When the Houthies in Yemen attacked Saudi Arabia, they would not attack back, because the Houthies are Arab too. They did not unite to fight other Arabs. The foreign ministers of the Arab world sat with Turkey, Pakistan, Indonesia and Malaysia and built a mechanism to follow Israel’s every move in East Jerusalem. They united to take down Netanyahu.

Right now only three of them signed. Don’t think the others will not join. One day Amalek is going to go bomb one of them, all of them are going to rise up, and there is nothing America can do about it. America can control them now only because they are not really united.

“Also the Carmanians raging in wrath shall go forth as the wild boars”. The Carmanians are Iran. Iran is not on the list, because Iran is not Arab: Iran is a Muslim country, but they are Persians. When these Arab countries rise up, Iran is going to join them. That is the war spoken of here.

“And with great power shall they come”: Iran will get that weapon. It does not matter what Trump says, what social media says or what the white man says. The scripture says they will get it, and there is nothing anybody can do about it. Iran has already attacked the American bases in every one of these countries except Lebanon, Palestine and Yemen, to turn America blind.

They “join battle with them”, with the dragons of Arabia, “and shall waste a portion of the land of the Assyrians.” The Assyrian here is Amalek, the Israeli. They are going to destroy that country.

This thing is closer than you think. Some think there are another fifty or a hundred years; the Most High is going to make it go so fast it will make your head spin. The Israelites are the only ones teaching this prophecy; no pastor teaches it. Stay in the Bible and do not go back to the Christian church. Watch and pray: pay attention to the news and your surroundings, especially the men, because you are the leaders, and you cannot lead clueless. Know a little bit about everything, and stop waiting on the major media to show you these things.

“Keep thy heart with all diligence; for out of it are the issues of life.” The heart is the mind. Keep your mind with all diligence, because out of your mind are the issues of life.

That is where destructive behavior among our people begins. Trauma is an emotional or physical response to a deeply distressing event that overwhelms a person’s ability to cope, and some in the truth use their trauma as an excuse to do horrible things: to destroy their marriage, their children, their job, this congregation, their brothers and sisters. Destructive behavior is any action that causes harm to yourself or your future: self harm and substance abuse (alcohol, drugs, money, sex), isolating yourself, procrastination, sabotaging your own career and your own relationships. You are your own biggest enemy, and if you are an enemy to yourself, you are an enemy to the man next to you.

The root of it is pain you never dealt with. Men hold it inside and bring it with them into the truth. A brother whose marriage in the world went bad brings that trauma into his marriage with a sister he spent three years pursuing, and convinces himself it wasn’t him who sabotaged his marriage in the world, it was her. No, negro, it was you. He never healed from it. Some sisters hold a thing for four days of atonement because they do not understand what it means to repent or to forgive, and you cannot forgive anyone else if you never forgave yourself. Low self-worth makes a sister with three kids settle for the most wicked-ass negro, and that is the one who is going to destroy her.

Self harm is not only a knife or a gun. Smoking the joint you know will hurt you is self harm. Drinking when you know you cannot hold your drink, then driving, is self harm. Marrying a sister you know is toxic, ignoring every red flag, marrying a brother when leadership told you his spirit is not right: that is self harm. Punching your husband while he drives with the baby in the back seat; feeding the dog and the chickens but telling your wife to go fetch food for herself: that is self-destruct. If you did not love that sister, why did you marry her? Why didn’t you just leave her the hell alone? You came into her life to destroy her because you never let go of your old trauma.

So examine yourself, and be honest with yourself and with the Most High. Judas Iscariot was never honest with himself. He knew he was a thief, and he never went to Christ and said, pray for me so I can get over that spirit.

“Search me, O God, and know my heart”: search me, Lord, and know my mind, because all evil thought starts with the mind.

“Try me, and know my thoughts”. To try is to prove. You are asking the Most High to prove you and look at your thoughts.

“And see if there be any wicked way in me”: look whether I have any evil in me, Most High.

“And lead me in the way everlasting.” That is talking about repentance: to change.

precepts.why:
“The law of the Lord is perfect”. The law of God is pure; there is nothing wrong with the law. And it is “converting the soul”: it changes you. Only the law can change you, and that is the way everlasting the Most High leads you in when you repent.

I used to be a murderer; the law said I shall not murder. I used to be a thief; the law said I shall not steal. I used to be an abuser. Once I knew the law, I repented. It is the same thing for the brother and the sister with trauma. Stop using your trauma as a crutch. Something that happened when you were fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, and now you are forty-six, fifty, in your third marriage, still using that garbage. You cannot keep a man or keep a woman because you cannot cope.

Identify the attitudes and behaviors that can destroy your spiritual growth, your relationships, your leadership and the unity. Some come in here to destroy that. The evil spirit on them does not like the unity of the brotherhood, because in the world there is always chaos: you never see a room full of black people with no fight and no argument, dancing, having a good time, breaking scriptures and breaking bread together. Whoever comes to destroy that is going to find himself outside these doors. Whatever you went through in the world, get over it quick, because it will destroy you.

sense.text:
We never grew up around order, structure and unity. So when we come around it, it makes us uncomfortable, because sometimes we realize we are the problem: we are the reason an environment becomes toxic and people bicker and fight, because we have an instigating spirit, the thing we grew up seeing. In a body and a truth where the light shines on that, you are forced to change, and many brothers and sisters do not want to.

“Whoso feareth the Lord shall direct his friendship aright: for as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.” If you fear the Lord you will direct your friendships aright, because as you are, so shall your neighbour be. If you are constantly having issues and problems, who is the one causing the trouble? With the laws of God and all the examples in the scriptures, you should be able to direct your friendships aright. So why is your name always in something?

“My son, gather instruction from thy youth up”. We did not have that. We did not have the opportunity to gather wisdom from our youth up, so we have to be born again coming into this truth and begin to do it now. You cannot drag in the way your grandmama and your auntie used to deal with each other. It is a new day. “So shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.”

This is for the toxic people. Wisdom “is very unpleasant to the unlearned.” You never learned about yourself. All you ever did was point out other people’s problems; you never examined yourself or looked in the mirror. So when wisdom finally reveals who you are, it is very unpleasant.

“He that is without understanding will not remain with her.” That is why people find a reason to leave. They get offended, they find a reason to be mad, and they go. The root of it is that they do not want to change once that wisdom is revealed.

Destructive attitudes begin internally before they become visible externally. A person may still attend services, teach, lead, pray or serve while harboring the wrong spirit. You look at the fringes and think, he’s good, she’s good. You would be surprised how many evil spirits are in the midst of us: brothers and sisters here every Sabbath and every new moon, brothers who teach who should not teach, who lead men, who pray with us, harboring the wrong spirit, and the wrong spirit means an evil spirit.

“A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” Out of the abundance of the mind the mouth speaks. Whatever comes out of the mouth comes from the mind.

precepts.why:
“For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he”. What a man is in his mind is what he is, and what comes out of him.

There is an old saying in the world: hang out with a thief long enough and eventually you will become a thief. You can be the most loyal man, never stole anything in your life, but your best friend is a thief. There are brothers who are married but whose circle is all single men; a brother who is an officer of fifty but never keeps company with the officers of fifty, only the soldiers of his ten.

“Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart is not with thee.” You attract what you are.

sense.text: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.” Pride goes before destruction, and an evil, haughty spirit before a fall.

precepts.why:
“Whoso loveth instruction loveth knowledge”: if you love instruction, you love knowledge. “But he that hateth reproof is brutish.” A brute is a savagely violent person or animal: a savage, a beast, a monster. Brutish is to be like that. The one who hates to be corrected is a beast.

That is pride, and here are the signs of it. Nobody can tell me anything: the know-it-all brother, the brother you can never tell anything because he already knows. Why are they correcting me? That is pride. I deserve a higher position: we saw that in the reconstruction we just did. Why is this brother over me, when two years ago he got caught in adultery? That is pride. He is over you because you have no idea what this is about.

sense.text:
Uzziah is one of the people in the Bible who were prideful. “But when he was strong, his heart was lifted up to his destruction”. Uzziah became strong, and he was no longer thinking the Most High God was doing these things; he thought he was doing them himself. He got very prideful and big-headed. We see some of that here, heads getting big.

“For he transgressed against the Lord his God”: he sinned against God, “and went into the temple of the Lord to burn incense upon the altar of incense.” Uzziah was of Judah. Who was supposed to burn incense? Levi. He got so prideful and big-headed that he went into the temple and tried to burn incense himself.

“And Azariah the priest went in after him, and with him fourscore priests of the Lord”, and “they withstood Uzziah the king”: all the priests said, what are you doing? “It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense”. It is not your job to burn incense to the Lord; it is the priests’ job. “Go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed”.

“Then Uzziah was wroth”. The priests told him to get out, that was not his job, and because he was the king he got angry. He argued with the priests: I am the king, I don’t want to hear it. “And while he was wroth with the priests, the leprosy even rose up in his forehead before the priests in the house of the Lord, from beside the incense altar.” See what the Most High did to him: covered him with leprosy.

“They thrust him out from thence; yea, himself hasted also to go out, because the Lord had smitten him.” God smote him because of pride.

“And Uzziah the king was a leper unto the day of his death”. He died a leper, all because of pride. See what pride can get you. Success can test your character as much as hardship.

precepts.why: “Then all the people of Judah took Uzziah, who was sixteen years old, and made him king in the room of his father Amaziah.” Uzziah was of Judah. That is why verse 1 has to be read: a man of Judah, not Levi, went into the temple to burn incense, a work that belonged only to the priests.
“Moreover Uzziah built towers in Jerusalem”, at the corner gate and the valley gate, “and fortified them.” This is the strength Uzziah came into before his heart was lifted up.

“Moreover Uzziah had an host of fighting men, that went out to war by bands”. He had built towers and a great army. He became strong, and when he was strong his heart was lifted up to his destruction.

sense.text:
“He that is slow to wrath is of great understanding”. If you are one of the brothers that is slow to anger, you have great understanding: in the Bible, the scriptures, the law. Some of you have what you call an anger issue, and you brought it into the truth with you. Two, three, four, five years sitting here and you have not gotten rid of it, and some use it as an excuse. We have seen it with men and with women.

“But he that is hasty of spirit”: the one who always gets angry about everything. Like Mike Tyson in the ring with his hands up to defend himself, some walk around the house like a boxer, waiting. The wife says shalom and you scream, why are you saying shalom to me? You bring your job home; leave that spirit outside the door before you walk into the house. Sisters too: he kisses you before work and you say, my first husband never kissed me, what do you want? He offers to take you out and you think he must want something. The brother or sister tries to do something good for you, and because of your past relationship you cannot receive it. Those are the things we see in the truth, because you never let go of the past.

If you are like that in the house with your wife or husband, you will be the same with the brothers and sisters, the same in the street, and the same with your kids: she is on punishment, she can have pancakes but no syrup; he can have salad but no salad dressing. Something is wrong with you, brother. You come home with food for yourself, the cats, the dog and the chickens and none for your wife, and you think it is normal. That is serious trauma, and we try to help you, dumb ass, and you look at us like we are the crazy ones. Seven, eight years here and still dealing with the same thing, and you tell the Bishop you can lead ten men. You treat your wife and children like that and think you can lead men? Examine your mind.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath”. Slow to wrath means slow to anger. As a leader you have to be able to control your spirit, and if you do it at home you will do it here too.

“For the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.” That anger spirit, that anger issue, does not come from the Most High. It comes from the devil. You have the devil on you, brother; you are working with Satan once you cannot control it, because you have had countless years to work on that spirit and you keep telling yourself you do not have it.

You cannot fix something if you do not admit it is broken. Until you admit to yourself, I am broken and this needs to be fixed, it is not going anywhere, and you will be fighting the same spirit five, six, seven years after you first came through that door. Some think admitting it makes them weak, or not a man. This is a hospital. Nobody goes to the hospital just to say hi to the doctor. The doctor examines you and prescribes the medication; if you never pick it up and come back two weeks later with the same problem asking for the same prescription, you are a nutcase. This book is the medication, the most powerful dose on the planet, and you can only heal if you take it. Nobody here can force you, not the Bishop, not the Captain. That is why some get the same counsel every week: we give you the medicine and you do not take it.

The signs of an anger problem: constant arguing; harsh speech, when you don’t have to speak harshly to your spouse all the time (learn to turn it off and on, like the teaching voice in the street); overreacting, blowing up one little thing like an atomic bomb; refusing forgiveness, a big one among black people, who forgive the white man quick but cannot forgive each other; and revenge-driven decisions.

sense.text:
“Be ye angry, and sin not”. You can get angry, but sin not. Between you and your wife, you can be angry with her by correcting her, you can argue with her, but don’t put your hands on her. Learn how to keep your damn hands to yourself. That is one thing that is not tolerated here in IC. Brothers are giving you their daughters; put your hands on one and I’ll let that brother whoop your ass, and some of you need it. Nothing a sister says should make you put your hands on her. If you had that spirit in the world, leave it outside that door. Sisters too: some sisters put their hands on their husbands, and that is not tolerated either. If you have that spirit, learn to control it.

“Let not the sun go down upon your wrath”. You have an argument on a Friday, before the Sabbath. Some love holding grudges even after the person apologized: she said, I was wrong, I’m sorry, and you are still mad. You want the Most High to forgive you, but you will not forgive your wife or your husband. That makes no sense. Do not let the sun go down: I accept your apology, I forgive you, it was a misunderstanding.

You are quick to forgive Bob, the white man at your job, but the one you are one flesh with, you hold a grudge against for years, and years later you bring it back up: remember the potato in the backyard? We are talking about bananas. You both stand before us asking the Most High to forgive you while holding grudges against each other in the same house. Forgive the wife or the husband sitting next to you first.
“Neither give place to the devil.” See what happens when you hold grudges and cannot forgive: you give place for Satan to come in.

“Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. Bitterness develops hatred, and hatred is actually murder. That goes back to trauma. Some hold bitterness so long that it starts affecting their health, the way they think and the way they look at things. A wife or a brother does something to you, you hold the bitterness, and you never look at that person the same. You wait for something to happen so you can use that spirit to get out of the situation; you use it as an excuse to do evil to each other. You hate the woman in the same bed with you every night, and she does not even know you hold bitterness against her. It has been so long that she forgot what she did, and so long that you forgot too: Deacon, I hate her because she did something, I just don’t remember what. Something is wrong with you, negro.

The spirit of bitterness manifested in 2018 in IUIC: people holding things for so long that one day they just snapped.

Bitterness alters your mind. It traps you in past hurts: something that happened years ago keeps you in that hurt, in that trauma, in that cage, and that is why you cannot cope. It skews your view of others: you have bitterness toward a brother, you put that seed in your wife, and now she looks at his wife differently, though it never had anything to do with her, and now there is division on that side too. It feeds a constant cycle of stress. And it shifts your focus toward cynicism, the inclination to believe people are motivated purely by self-interest. Bitterness puts things there that are not there: the brother who told the captain, I think you think I’m gay; Deacon, I think you think I’m a thief. How do you know what I think? That is bitterness changing how you think and react every single day. That is a miserable life, never at peace.

Bitterness is a hidden root that eventually produces visible damage. The signs of it, between you and your wife: repeatedly revisiting the offense; speaking negatively about the offender; difficulty praying for each other or for others; refusing reconciliation; and generalized mistrust of others.

precepts.why:
There is no way to live a life of bitterness and grow in this truth, become a better spouse, or retain the precepts that help you gain the kingdom of heaven while that bitterness is in you.

“Follow peace with all men”. Following peace is the same as endeavoring to keep the unity. It takes effort. You cannot follow peace and at the same time be harboring and nourishing hatred; the two do not work together. “And holiness”: keeping the commandments of God, not letting the sun go down on your wrath. “Without which no man shall see the Lord.” You cannot hate your brother whom you can see and say you love God whom you cannot see. God says you won’t have to worry about seeing me, because I died for the person you are harboring hatred against. He forgave that person many days of atonement ago, and you are still holding on to the thing they fasted for.

Then verse 15: “lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you”. First it troubles you, “and thereby many be defiled”: then it spreads. The skewed way you see a sister, a brother, or leadership, you begin to spread to others who did not see them that way at first, and you become like Esau. A lot of times the white man is the devil, absolutely, and a lot of times our people are coons, a thousand percent. But in these classes your salvation is on the line.

“Let all bitterness, and wrath, and anger, and clamour, and evil speaking, be put away from you, with all malice”. God says put all of these away from you.

“And be ye kind one to another”. Some know how to be kind to that nation but not to their own wife, their own husband, or each other. Be kind one to another: honor one another, respect one another, love one another. “Tenderhearted, forgiving one another, even as God for Christ’s sake hath forgiven you.”

You are supposed to pray three times a day, and every time you ask the Most High for forgiveness. But in the same house you have not forgiven your spouse, and you have not forgiven the brother sitting next to you, and still you pray three times a day for forgiveness. That is insanity; God is not listening to anything you say. The atonement just passed and another is coming in a couple of months. Whatever they did to you, you have held it for years. Don’t you think it is time to forgive them before that day comes?

Trauma says, why does everybody in my life always hurt me, always take advantage of me? It is always his fault, always her fault. Some are in their third or fourth marriage with the same problem they had in the other three. Examine yourself, brother. Examine yourself, sis.

sense.text:
Now jealousy and envy. “A sound heart is the life of the flesh”. The sound heart is the mind: a sound mind, the right mind, is the life of the body. When you are in the right mind you can do a lot. Sometimes you cannot even fall asleep because you are not in a sound mind; you let little things bother you. Stress is what is going to kill some of you, not this truth, because you stress about everything and never have a peaceful mind. The whole body starts with a peaceful mind. You did not come here for drama; you came here for peace. God is a God of peace. When you pray, ask Him for peace in your household, in your wife, in your husband. If you do not have peace in the mind, the rest of the body has no peace.

“But envy the rottenness of the bones.” You are your own enemy. Yes, the white man is the devil, but he cannot keep one of us here from getting the kingdom. Only you can keep you from getting it. Only you can remove your name from the book of life; the white man does not have that power, but you do. So who are you fighting against? Yourself. That is self-destruct, and that is why I am staying the hell away from some of you.

This is what jealousy and envy did between Saul and David. They came back from war, “when David was returned from the slaughter of the Philistine”, and the women came out “singing and dancing, to meet king Saul”. Everybody was enjoying themselves, happy because they won. “And the women answered one another as they played, and said, Saul hath slain his thousands, and David his ten thousands.”

Saul was the king, and David was basically in the military, under Saul. If the Deacon and the Captain go to war and the people say the Captain killed more, why should the Deacon get mad? He is over the Captain. The Captain looking good makes the Deacon look good. When a young brother breaks a scripture well at camp, say, good job, keep up the good work, young man. Who did he learn from? You. You should walk in here with a smile on your face, not get mad.

But that wasn’t Saul. “And Saul was very wroth, and the saying displeased him”: “They have ascribed unto David ten thousands, and to me they have ascribed but thousands: and what can he have more but the kingdom? And Saul eyed David from that day and forward.” That was the farthest thing from David’s mind. David loved Saul and just wanted to be around him, and Saul did not understand that.

In this truth the Most High will always send a brother to help you. To Moses He sent Joshua, and to Elijah He sent Elisha. He sent David to make Saul look good: a king needs a strong military, and David was a mighty man. Saul did not recognize it and let jealousy and envy overtake him, and some of us have that spirit right now.

A leader never raises another leader to be like himself; a leader raises other leaders to be greater than himself. The young men walking around here, fifteen to twenty years old, are the future leaders. You want your own sons to be better than you and not to struggle like you did; it should be the same here. We are the going leaders, they are the coming leaders, and our job is to prepare them for the fight that is coming. Do not let jealousy and envy overtake you so that you cannot see the vision. The vision is to find the twelve tribes of Israel and bring them back. Never go left or right from it.

Some have envy and jealousy against the wife or husband in the same house, competing with each other: she makes more money than me. You’re an idiot. Get yourself together, go to school, but do not envy her. The two become one.

“The evil spirit from God came upon Saul”, and “there was a javelin in Saul’s hand.” See what jealousy and envy did. “And Saul cast the javelin”: Saul tried to kill him, just because the people said David killed ten thousand and Saul a thousand, when in reality David made Saul look good. Saul could not accept it.

Some have that spirit: me, me, me, why can’t I be me? This is bigger than you. Anybody who walks in here from the street, you are responsible for them. You are sent to wake up the twelve tribes; do your damn job. That selfish spirit does the most stupid thing, gets put out, and never considers that his wife is close with the sisters and that is all she has, that his children are close with the other children and that is all they have. You destroy your whole family because it is always about you. Get rid of that small mind.

Murmuring and complaining. If you don’t have a solution, shut the hell up. How is your complaining going to help me, or the men and women in this room? We want solutions. If you don’t have one, sit down, brother. And God does not want to hear you complain either.

“Do all things without murmurings and disputings”.

The chaos you grew up in becomes your default setting, so you gravitate toward people and places that produce the same chaos. That is why some cannot accept a wife or husband being nice to them, or brothers and sisters dancing and having a good time at the new moon: you are used to the club, people screaming and cursing each other. Your mind is not used to peace, so you work to turn a peaceful sister into a chaos sister, a peaceful brother into a chaos brother.

The old man goes to the back page of the book when you come into this truth, but he never left. If you hold on to him you will reach that back page and the old man will come out: Deacon, I just snapped.

The self-destructive behaviors no one talks about: sabotaging good relationships, lashing out and starting fights because your mind whispers that they will leave anyway; chasing the quick fix even when you know it is unhealthy. And isolating yourself out of shame. If you make a mistake and are put in regular clothes until you fix yourself, do not sit there ashamed: did you repent? The Most High forgave you. Shake the dust off, come back and sit down. Do not let a simple mistake take you out of the fight. When we call and you never pick up, it is not that you don’t care, it is that you are drowning in guilt. We don’t want to destroy you; we want you to come back, because men make mistakes.

Clinging to toxic relationships is insanity, like getting high and convincing yourself it is good when every time you get high you do something stupid. Leadership offers a sister with kids a good brother with a job, his own place and his own car, and she says, he’s not my type. Why? Because your type is toxic as hell. Your type gave you three kids and bounced. Then another sister scoops him up and now you are mad. You lost.

Telling yourself you are too broken to get better is that trauma. We are a broken people; nobody is more broken than us. The only thing that can fix us and make us whole is the Bible, not Christianity and not Islam. If you were a thief, a murderer or an adulterer, the Bible can fix you. The mind has a mind of its own and tells you things that are not there, and you believe it; I am my own biggest enemy. Tell your mind to shut the hell up.

Self-destructive behavior starts as a way to soothe the pain of trauma, and over time you grow a tolerance and need more of it. If you have no drama you cannot function, so you find a way to bring drama in. Like a fix, a needle: you have to bring some destruction in to feel normal. You stress over the mortgage, get high so you won’t think about it, come down, and the mortgage is still not paid, so you get high again. That is insanity, and that is self-destruct.

precepts.why:
The Most High hates murmuring. “How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me? I have heard the murmurings of the children of Israel, which they murmur against me.” “As truly as I live, saith the Lord, as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you”, “from twenty years old and upward, which have murmured against me, Doubtless ye shall not come into the land”. He killed every single one of those who murmured.

A murmuring spirit focuses on the problem instead of the solution, and a murmuring spirit never has a solution. Its effects: it weakens morale; it divides people and brings division; it discourages leadership, always murmuring about leadership; and it spreads negativity.
Murmuring weakens morale, divides the people, discourages leadership and spreads negativity, and “rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft.”

sense.text: So examine yourself: “Search me, O God, and know my heart: try me, and know my thoughts: And see if there be any wicked way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.”

Admit the issue you are facing. “He that covereth his sins shall not prosper: but whoso confesseth and forsaketh them shall have mercy.” Once you make that mistake, repent quick and keep it moving. That is what David did: he committed murder, repented quick and kept on moving. That is what we should do.
Repent. “Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord”.

Renew your mind. Your mind must be renewed, brothers and sisters, when you come into this truth; that is how you get rid of the old man. “And be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind”, by changing your mind and your thoughts, “that ye may prove what is that good, and acceptable, and perfect, will of God.”
Control your words. “Death and life are in the power of the tongue”. You have the power to destroy and the power to build; it is up to you. “And they that love it shall eat the fruit thereof.”

precepts.why:
“Even so the tongue is a little member, and boasteth great things. Behold, how great a matter a little fire kindleth!” “And the tongue is a fire, a world of iniquity”, it “defileth the whole body, and setteth on fire the course of nature; and it is set on fire of hell.” Every kind of beast is tamed of mankind, “But the tongue can no man tame; it is an unruly evil, full of deadly poison.”

“Therewith bless we God, even the Father”: with that same mouth you bless God and ask for forgiveness, “and therewith curse we men”, the brother and the sister sitting next to you, “which are made after the similitude of God.” That brother next to you is made after the image of God. “Out of the same mouth proceedeth blessing and cursing.”

The tongue is the most powerful tool. You can destroy a brother with it or you can build a brother with it. Pick building a brother.

sense.text: Forgive. “Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another”. If you don’t forgive one another, don’t expect the Most High to forgive you either. They go hand in hand.

We all should have the mind of Christ. “Let this mind be in you, which was also in Christ”.

Past hurt is used, manipulated, to justify present anger. Here is what is destructive and what is Christlike: pride is destructive, and humility is Christlike; anger, and self-control; bitterness, and forgiveness; jealousy, and contentment; rebellion, and obedience; selfishness, and service, because we are servants; murmuring, and gratitude; hatred, and love; impatience, and patience; harshness, and gentleness; division, and unity; arrogance, and being teachable.
